openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI radio anatomy consulted directly — union built from the three clones: Salt's RadioButton + RadioButtonGroup (a real <fieldset role="radiogroup"> wrapper distributing disabled/readOnly/validationStatus/value/name via RadioGroupContext to any number of RadioButton children, each a <label> wrapping a real, visually-hidden native <input type="radio"> plus a RadioButtonIcon <div> plus label text as a sibling child — the same label-IS-the-whole-clickable-region shell checkbox/switch already used), shadcn's RadioGroup + RadioGroupItem (a bare Radix RadioGroupPrimitive.Root — [R] a <div role="radiogroup"> per the linked docs — wrapping any number of RadioGroupPrimitive.Item children, each [R] a <button role="radio"> with NO owned label, plus a conditionally-rendered Indicator holding one lucide CircleIcon glyph), and M3's <md-radio> (a Lit custom element with NO group wrapper of any kind — each radio manages its OWN shadow DOM: a <div class="container"> holding an <md-ripple>, an <md-focus-ring>, and an <svg class="icon"> with two circles (a masked outer ring, a scaling inner dot) — and NO native <input> anywhere; selection sharing across radios with the same `name` attribute is done entirely in JS by a SingleSelectionController querying the host's ROOT NODE, deliberately built to 'mimic native <input type="radio"> behavior' per its own doc comment).

behavior.pattern: A single-selection control for choosing exactly one option from a small, fully-exposed set, per the W3C APG radio pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/), which Salt's own usage.mdx cites directly. THE HEADLINE STRUCTURAL QUESTION THIS MATRIX HAD TO ANSWER FIRST: does a 'radio-group' need a group wrapper element at all? The answer is genuinely split three ways. Salt: YES, a real, separate <fieldset role="radiogroup"> component (RadioButtonGroup) that a RadioButton can also be used WITHOUT (a standalone RadioButton reads its own checked/name props directly) [S]. shadcn: YES, and MANDATORY — RadioGroupItem has no meaning without a RadioGroup ancestor providing the Radix context that supplies its `checked`/`onCheckedChange` derivation from a shared `value` (there is no useful standalone RadioGroupItem) [S/R]. M3: NO GROUP ELEMENT EXISTS AT ALL — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly across radio.ts, radio-styles, and the whole radio/ directory: no radiogroup role, no fieldset, no wrapping custom element. Each <md-radio> is independently self-sufficient; selection-sharing is a purely DOM-query-based side effect of multiple radios sharing one `name` attribute in the same root node, driven by SingleSelectionController — a mechanism the controller's own doc comment says is deliberately built to 'mimic native <input type="radio"> behavior', which is the OPPOSITE of Salt's/shadcn's own component-tree/context-based sharing [S]. This chassis therefore models `structure.group` as a LOCKED config row whose M3 value is a real, distinct strategy (`name-scoped`) rather than an absence, because M3 clearly HAS a working group mechanism — it just is not an element. Two further axes carry real character: (1) THE SELECTION-CHECK MECHANISM — Salt and shadcn compare a GROUP-held string `value` against each item's own `value` prop (a value-driven model, context-shared); M3 gives each radio its OWN independent boolean `checked` property and UNCHECKS ITS SIBLINGS IMPERATIVELY the instant it becomes checked (an item-driven model, DOM-query-shared) — genuinely different data flow, not merely different syntax; (2) NATIVE INPUT PRESENCE — Salt [S] and, by declared union, this chassis's shadcn approximation [R] both use a REAL native <input type="radio">; M3 uses NONE AT ALL, the first time in this whole pipeline (checkbox and switch's own M3 columns BOTH had a real native input) that M3 diverges from its own established pattern — M3 sets ARIA role/checked purely through ElementInternals in JS (`this[internals].role = 'radio'`, `this[internals].ariaChecked = String(this.checked)`), never touching a form-control DOM node the way its sibling components do.
behavior.chassis: skeleton/radio-group.tsx — written from the template's part union: a RadioGroup component (a <fieldset role="radiogroup">, a <div role="radiogroup">, or a bare unwrapped <div> per structure.group's three strategies) providing a React context to any number of RadioItem children, each a root (a real <label> when structure.shell="label-wrap", a plain <span> otherwise) wrapping a real native <input type="radio"> (always — matching Salt exactly and a declared, reasonable API-shape union for shadcn/M3, the SAME 'let the browser do the work it already offers' choice checkbox.tsx and switch.tsx already made for shadcn specifically, extended here to M3 too since M3 is the outlier THIS time) and a dot <span> containing the glyph per structure.dot's three strategies. DOM SHAPE, decided DELIBERATELY BEFORE writing a single selector, per CLAUDE.md rule 12 and CHECKBOX-MATRIX.md findings 10/11: <input> and <dot> are rendered as SIBLINGS, both direct children of the item root — this matches Salt's REAL DOM exactly (RadioButton.tsx: <label><input/><RadioButtonIcon/>{label}</label>, input and icon are siblings, confirmed by reading the file, not assumed). EVERY conditional style rule (checked/hover/focus/pressed/disabled/readonly/validation) is written as `[data-slot="radio-item"]:has([data-slot="radio-input"]:STATE) [data-slot="radio-dot"]` or `...[data-slot="radio-item"]` directly — anchoring `:has()` at the ITEM ROOT (the one ancestor guaranteed to contain both input and dot as descendants), never assuming adjacency. A SECOND DECLARED SIMPLIFICATION, distinct from checkbox/switch's chassis notes: because this chassis renders a REAL native `<input type="radio">` sharing one `name` per group in EVERY column (including M3, which has none in its real source), the browser's OWN native radio-group keyboard semantics (Tab moves to the checked radio or the first one; arrow keys move focus AND selection among same-name siblings) apply FOR FREE in all three columns with zero custom keydown code — and this is not an arbitrary shortcut: M3's own SingleSelectionController exists SPECIFICALLY to reproduce that exact native behavior for a component that has no native input to get it from for free ('provides root node-scoped single selection for elements, similar to native <input type="radio"> selection', its own doc comment), so approximating M3 with a real native input converges on the SAME observable keyboard behavior its real JS controller was written to imitate, rather than inventing an unrelated one. VERIFICATION CAVEAT, stated plainly per rule 12: see the matrix doc's closing finding for whether a live browser render confirmed this session's selectors.

THE SECOND HEADLINE ROW. Salt [S]: NATIVE — accessibility.mdx: 'Up/Down/Left/Right moves focus between the available radio button options, and simultaneously selects an option' — no JS in RadioButton.tsx/RadioButtonGroup.tsx implements this; it is the browser's own built-in behaviour for same-name sibling `<input type="radio">` elements, entirely free. shadcn [R]: presumed roving-tabindex behaviour implemented in Radix's own JS, per the general Radix primitives pattern and the linked docs; not independently confirmable without primitives/ cloned. M3 [S]: EXPLICIT, real, sourced JS — `SingleSelectionController.handleKeyDown` listens for ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, computes the next non-disabled sibling sharing the SAME `name` attribute (querying the connected ROOT NODE, RTL-aware via `getComputedStyle(...).direction`), unchecks/blurs every other sibling, checks+focuses the target, and dispatches a `change` event — with the controller's OWN doc comment stating the intent directly: 'similar to native <input type="radio"> selection'. THIS CHASSIS REPRODUCES ALL THREE OBSERVABLY FOR FREE: because every column renders a REAL native `<input type="radio">` sharing one `name` per group (see structure.native-input's declared union for M3), the BROWSER's own native arrow-key/Tab semantics apply identically in all three columns with zero custom keydown code in skeleton/radio-group.tsx — which is not an arbitrary shortcut, since M3's own controller was written SPECIFICALLY to imitate that exact native behaviour for a component with no native input to inherit it from.

HOW the 'only one checked' invariant is enforced differs by DATA FLOW, not merely syntax. Salt [S] and shadcn [R]: a GROUP-held string `value` (RadioButtonGroupProps.value / RadioGroupPrimitive.Root's `value`) is compared against each item's own `value` prop — `radioGroupChecked = checkedProp ?? (radioGroup && value ? radioGroup.value === value : checkedProp)` (RadioButton.tsx) — a single source of truth living in the GROUP, propagated down via context; changing selection means changing ONE piece of shared state. M3 [S]: each `<md-radio>` owns its OWN independent boolean `checked` property; when one becomes checked, `SingleSelectionController.handleCheckedChange()` IMPERATIVELY sets every OTHER same-name sibling's `.checked = false` directly — there is no single shared piece of state anywhere, only N independent booleans kept mutually exclusive by an uncheck-siblings side effect. This chassis implements the Salt/shadcn (group-value) model as its single internal engine, which is OBSERVABLY equivalent for all three columns (exactly one item ends up checked after any interaction) even though M3's own real implementation arrives there by a structurally different route — a declared simplification, not a fabricated behaviour, since the OUTCOME every real system converges on is what a consumer of this registry actually experiences.
